Silence Wave creates a cast-denial window before an enemy uses an important ability. Land the projectile as your team is ready to commit, then punish while escape or defensive casts are restricted. A silence is not a universal answer to an already-running channel.

Silence Wave or Cursed Relic can deny Doorway’s reset while your team can finish. Warp Stone and movement investment help with dangerous exit geometry, while Counterspell answers an important incoming hit. Keep a response for the second part of the sequence rather than using every defensive resource at entry.

Silence Wave or Cursed Relic can deny Soul Exchange during a coordinated finish. Add anti-heal when Life Drain or healing items keep Lady Geist alive; Spirit Resilience fits repeated spell pressure. Metal Skin is conditional on a weapon-focused build, not a response to her drain or health swap.

Silence Wave or Cursed Relic can deny the defensive reset during a coordinated finish. Prepare Counterspell for Affliction’s application or Divine Barrier for its removal role. Spirit Resilience helps repeated spirit pressure, but mobility denial and the ultimate response still serve separate jobs.

Silence Wave or Cursed Relic can prevent Soul Exchange before Lady Geist casts it, while Counterspell is a timing-sensitive response to the application. Keep the finish at a safe distance if you cannot read the cast reliably. Anti-heal reduces recovery, but it does not simply cancel a health swap.

Counterspell serves a separate timed role against a readable Power Slash, and anti-heal reduces recovery without canceling the protective state.
